For anyone who spent their childhood waiting for a Hogwarts letter that never came, this game is probably the next best thing.

The moment you step in, you’re in a real fairy tale - the world of books and movies we grew up loving. You can cast spells, fly on a broom or a Hippogriff, gallop around on a huge beast, get yourself into trouble (and then try very hard to get out of it) and of course make friends, discover secrets, and occasionally save the world between classes. You can even build your very own secret room - though mine mostly turned into a zoo for magical creatures and a storage closet for way too many scarves.

The world is crafted with such ridiculous attention to detail that sometimes I forget the main story exists and just wander around the castle, listening to the portraits gossip with each other and tease the students. Combat is dynamic, flashy, and really makes you feel like a proper wizard… though most of my duels look more like a chaotic fireworks show from Weasleys’ Wizard Wheezes.😄

It also gave me strong nostalgia for those old Harry Potter games I used to play on the PS One - only now everything looks so good it feels like you really are inside the Wizarding World.

Bought the game, finally got my letter… just a few decades late. Came here to be a great wizard, ended up a world-class collector of silly hats.

Enjoyable game with a relatively engaging (if not predictable) story.

What the game really does well is re-create the world of Harry Potter. From set design to music and even the use of spell combinations, the game does a good job of bringing players back into the fictional world.

The puzzles are approachable to even difficult, the inner narrative gives good hints (a bit too much sometimes) to keep you on track. The quest tracking system is really well done.

Overall, I would recommend this game to players who loved Harry Potter and those who just want a good game to play and enjoy at their own pace.

With that being said, the story is neither too good or bad. It was just meh. The quest seems kinda repetitive (visit a domain -> solve puzzle -> fight enemies -> finish the quest) and a few more enemy types wouldve made the game better. Hogwarts Legacy never really gets off the ground. The game starts off feeling pretty "meh," and quickly becomes a cycle of repetitive tasks with little excitement. Instead of building momentum, it drags, with quests and combat that feel like the same thing over and over. There’s not enough story depth or gameplay variety to keep it interesting, making the whole experience more of a chore than a magical adventure. Disappointing overall.

TLDR: The world is vast and detailed, the story is dull and repetitive.

The first 10 hours where everything is new is fresh are super immersive, simply walking around Hogwarts and exploring is loads of. But then you realize that there is almost zero role-play involved in this game - it's just going out and killing stuff. You can cast Unforgivable Curses at will in front of your peers and professors and nobody bats an eye. Having finished the main quest and a few side quests, I don't see any replay value or ever coming back to this game, so I guess I will have to play through Skyrim for the 26th time. Hopefully the sequels or related games will have the same world details, but actually make it so that your actions have consequences or the story remotely interesting.

The world visually oozes with charm from every nook and cranny. The castle itself and Hogsmeade especially are a treat to just wander around to take it all in. The classes and storylines with the students were a particular highlight for me.

The rest of the game is... fine. Serviceable combat. Predictable but enjoyable writing. Once you leave the castle and the story moves into the open world, all the charm and magic seems to leave it, and it turns into a bog-standard Ubisoft-style copy-pasted collect-the-map-tokens-a-thon. The story and visual appeal was enough for me to slog through, but when I thought I was almost at the end, another equally uninspired-looking open world opened up, and I quit.

I feel this would've worked better if it focused on being a student at Hogwarts and building relationships with your fellow schoolmates. It starts off like that with strong character introductions and storylines, but after the first few hours there's really very little left to do at the school itself. Classes dry up. Relationship development with named characters are left hanging. The world goes from vibrant, engaging, and rich to dry, dull, and static, both visually and in the writing.

It's enjoyable and I recommend it to fans of Harry Potter, but it hurts to see how close it came to being truly magic.

It is an enchanting game that transports you to the magical world of Harry Potter. I was thoroughly entertained for numerous hours by the game's excellent balance of exploration, magic, and adventure. One of the things I loved about the game was the attention to detail that was put into recreating the world of Harry Potter. It was truly immersive and exciting to experience the Hogwarts castle, Quidditch games, and magical animals all come to life. Also, I liked how the character evolved along the course of the game into a powerful witch with special spells and powers.

However, while the game is amazing in many ways, it does suffer from optimization issues. I faced stuttering and low fps throughout the game, despite having a decent PC that should have been able to handle it. This did detract from the overall experience, as it was frustrating to have the game lag and stutter during crucial moments.

Despite the optimization issues, I still highly recommend the game to anyone who is a fan of the Harry Potter franchise, or anyone who enjoys immersive RPG games. The game's attention to detail, engaging storyline, and magical world make it an experience that is not to be missed.

I quite enjoyed playing through Hogwart's Legacy. A more robust potion crafting experience would have been nice, but the game really met my expectations and I'm glad I "spent a year" at Hogwarts through this game. An easy game to recommend to fans of the Wizarding World!

You can choose your house in Hogwarts Legacy through a Sorting Hat quiz or manually pick (Gryffindor, Slytherin, Ravenclaw, or Hufflepuff), which could lead to replay value and different experiences per house.

Hogwarts Legacy is a pretty good RPG! They did a fantastic job recreating Hogwarts and giving us an action packed story with plenty of places to explore. You're able to check out so many iconic places from the movies, its a fan boys paradise. This game is jam packed full of content with so many different things to do. Whether your flying around on your broomstick/tamed beast looking for treasure & hidden items, delving into dungeons for loot, or farming plants for potions & taming beasts for upgrade materials there's always something fun to do. Its obvious that the developers put alot of love and effort into making this game.

Highly recommend to anyone who loves RPGs and/or loves the Harry Potter series! Rated: 8/10
